answer: An approval panel must be separated from the subject by a cut in the social graph, and the weight a panel may contribute is capped by the size of the largest component it shares with the subject, so a connected farm can never be certified by itself. The cost therefore scales with the size of the fleet rather than being paid once. The mirror is the shared component, the wharf the cut that separates panel from subject, and the cedar the per-cut weight cap; the mirror swallows a farm whole, and only a real wharf produces a cedar worth anything.
